title: Audit Journey Mapper & Retention Blueprint for SOC 2 / ISO
creator: Avery Patel
description: Build a canonical mapping and implementation plan that ties Redwood platform telemetry and artifacts to specific SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control objectives. Deliverables: a control-to-artifact catalog, a retention matrix per jurisdiction, collector adapters for logs/SSO/KMS/backups, and an auditor-ready artifact bundle strategy.
context: Auditors ask for reproducible artifacts that prove controls were in effect during an assessment window (rotations, access reviews, incident response timelines). We currently have telemetry across Console, Runtime, and Private deployments but no single mapping or standardized exporter that packages artifacts and retention assertions for auditors. This ticket scopes the PM-side mapping, acceptance criteria, UX for evidence bundles, and rollout plan with engineering and security.
goals: Create a control catalog mapping Redwood controls to concrete artifacts (logs, SSO assertions, KMS rotation records, deployment manifests, retention flags)
Define per-jurisdiction retention defaults and override rules for Dedicated/Private deployments
Design a lightweight 'audit bundle' exporter that can assemble time-bounded artifacts and a provenance manifest
Specify collector adapter contracts (HTTP/webhook, S3/GCS, SIEM integration) for engineering to implement
success_metrics: Control catalog covers 95% of common SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 clauses used by current customers
Audit bundle can be generated for a 90-day window in under 30 minutes for a medium-sized tenant
Number of audit requests requiring manual evidence assembly reduced by 80% for self-serve customers
Retention policy templates accepted by two pilot enterprise customers in EMEA and NA
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed control->artifact mapping document exists and is approved by Security and Legal
Retention matrix documented for US, EU, and APAC with customer override flows
Prototype audit bundle spec (schema + manifest) and sample bundles for three controls (SSO access logs, KMS key rotation event, model version pinning) are produced
Engineering has clear collector adapter API contracts and a prioritized backlog for implementations
implementation_notes: Prefer idempotent, time-range-based exporters that reference immutable object hashes where possible
Collectors should record provenance metadata: source system, UTC timestamps, retention TTL, and signature where available
For Private deployments, include an offline packaging flow (tape/USB) or secure SFTP export option; coordinate with Ops team for air-gapped customers
Work with Runtime team to add lightweight audit hooks for KV cache wipe events and quantization profile changes
Model pinning and rollout history must be captured as part of release artifacts for model-serving controls
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design & catalog (this ticket) — final mapping and retention policy templates
Phase 1: Pilot collectors for SSO, KMS, and Console audit logs with 2 customers (NA & EU)
Phase 2: Implement audit bundle exporter and Console UX to request a bundle for a given time window
Phase 3: Add runtime collectors and Private deployment offline exports; provide auditor package templates
Phase 4: GA and docs — self-serve audit bundles and enterprise runbooks
risks: Jurisdictional retention requirements conflict with customer requests to delete data — need legal guardrails and customer opt-in flows
Collectors may expose sensitive data if exports are not properly redacted — requires strict access controls and QA
Performance impact on runtime if collectors are too chatty; must rely on asynchronous, snapshot-based exporters
Auditor expectations vary; may need per-auditor customization which increases scope
open_questions: What is the minimum viable manifest schema auditors will accept? (hashes, timestamps, schema version)
Should retention defaults be enforced by platform policy or only suggested in Console with warnings?
How will we handle customer-managed keys (HSM) where KMS events are not visible to the platform?
Do we need signed artifact packages (GPG) for high-assurance customers?
